source_scope_proof.arm_report:
# Exact-row SIMD squared error

Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2 darwin/arm64 archsimd, PGO off, GOMAXPROCS=1.
Immediate parent 1e8809b63498b77fb6a347b0c085ebfe3c9aab49 (PR37), old assembly
691cd0512c4829d9ee40d483205dd223f9eb028d. Native speed only; Rosetta results
are correctness checks, never x64 performance evidence.

SSE8's bounded path proves h=1..64 and nonnegative strides<2^30, then checks
both final eight-byte row endpoints. Exact uint64 row loads need no padding,
including unaligned, zero-stride, overlapping or mutually aliased read-only
rows. Typed unsafe pointers stay live and are never retained or written.
Offsets and unused final increments fit int64. Larger heights and unusual
strides keep the original checked-slice fallback byte for byte, including
h1 with an unused negative or maximal stride and empty geometry behavior.

Pack two rows by inserting both uint64 lanes directly. Compute unsigned byte
Max-Min before widening: this is |a-b| in 0..255 for every ordered byte pair,
so squaring is exact. Separate low/high int32 sums cover each row once; an odd
tail accumulates only low8 bytes. At 64 rows total SSE<=33,292,800 fits int32.
No new AVX256 state, CPU requirements, assembly, dependencies or production cgo.

Fresh six balanced parent/assembly/current orders,100ms per 36 identical public
B.Loop fixtures. Four APIs, three strides 8/8,32/37,1312/1320, and random,
maximum-error, identical-pixel patterns. Exact visible spans, origins3/5,
independent per-pixel scalar SSE before/after timing and full backing canaries.
All samples allocate zero. Ranges below cover all three pixel patterns.

| Public API / strides | Parent/current time | Assembly/current time |
|---|---:|---:|
| slice8x4 / 8-8 | 1.2961–1.3112x | 2.2662–3.2790x |
| slice8x4 / 32-37 | 1.3021–1.3104x | 2.4183–3.1861x |
| slice8x4 / 1312-1320 | 1.3148–1.3170x | 2.5106–2.9633x |
| slice8x8 / 8-8 | 1.4807–1.4975x | 0.9947–1.0612x |
| slice8x8 / 32-37 | 1.4769–1.4926x | 0.9975–1.0682x |
| slice8x8 / 1312-1320 | 1.4875–1.4986x | 1.0009–1.0360x |
| slice8x16 / 8-8 | 1.6253–1.6354x | 0.8515–0.8718x |
| slice8x16 / 32-37 | 1.6294–1.6389x | 0.8551–0.8696x |
| slice8x16 / 1312-1320 | 1.6262–1.6423x | 0.8497–0.8646x |
| pointer8x8 / 8-8 | 1.4389–1.4465x | 0.6988–0.7076x |
| pointer8x8 / 32-37 | 1.4336–1.4452x | 0.6952–0.7108x |
| pointer8x8 / 1312-1320 | 1.4372–1.4535x | 0.6990–0.7016x |

All nine 8x16 cases qualify: median 1.6253–1.6423x parent;
all 54 paired samples exceed 1.5802x. Keep this correctness-verified
component gain independently of whole-codec changes. Other sizes remain
below 1.5x parent; eight/sixteen-row and pointer paths still include assembly
deficits. This does not establish blanket assembly parity.

Whole synthetic 1280x720 VP8, realtime CPU 8, 2500 kbps, one thread, six balanced
orders, separate from kernel timing (positive means more time/slower):

* 300 frames: -0.1075% versus parent (3/6 faster), +5.9503% versus old assembly (0/6 faster).

* 60 frames: +1.4459% versus parent (0/6 faster), +12.5059% versus old assembly (0/6 faster).

Fresh separate 60-frame follow-up: -0.6109% versus parent (5/6 faster), +9.4058% versus old assembly (0/6 faster). Retain both runs; do not replace the first regression with this follow-up.

All 23 non-timing fields and every allocation sample match, with zero allocations.
These output statistics do not assert bitstream identity. Shared-desktop timing
and varied assembly samples do not support causal/additive claims across runs.
The whole ARM assembly gap remains open. No libvpx C result is inferred from
these assembly comparisons; C has its own native CI job and quality scope.

Correctness: full native suite passes, ARM race/checkptr2 passes, x64 checkptr2
under Rosetta passes, and actual AVX-off fallback passes (SIMD-only tests
explicitly skip there). New tests exercise 720 disjoint +720 mutual-alias calls,
14 short-window panics, unused extreme strides, odd/boundary/fallback heights,
and every one of 65,536 ordered byte pairs in 512 eight-by-sixteen calls.
Independent static review verified arithmetic, endpoints, pointer lifetime,
odd tails, fallback equivalence and live benchmark scope. The first private
full-suite run lacked two upstream C control-table fixtures; both its failure
and the successful rerun with exact pinned fixture hashes are retained.
Refreshed PGO and repository gates are logged. Native x64 performance awaits
this successor PR's exact-head CI; its harness retains 246 controls and adds 36
public fixtures, both new source hashes and focused selected/race checks.

Every diagnostic, rejected variant, raw sample and source snapshot is retained.
The initial row-pointer-only change topped out below 1.5x. Four-row unrolling
alone did not qualify; byte absolute differences helped 16-row cases, and
removing the overwritten broadcast produced the selected winner. Fresh runs
confirm it independently of those exploratory measurements. Generated code
is diagnostic evidence, never a substitute for timing. No competing local
Go builds/tests/profiles ran during native measurements. README files are
untouched; experiment records belong here.

Successor integration: rebased onto PR #37's AMD widened-row repair
f3a02aee81979d0c822f5814343f2287d9d86194 before native submission. SSE source
is unchanged, and all 228 ARM SSE8 instruction words exactly match the timed
prototype. Combined AMD SSE/subpixel checkptr correctness passes under Rosetta;
PGO/fingerprint/noasm/SIMD-selection/pre-commit gates pass again. The rebased
validation archive preserves all logs and source hashes. Native x64 CI compares
this successor with that exact repaired parent; neither a cross-CPU comparison
nor the old uncorrected AMD vertical path is substituted as its baseline.

pr_snapshot.body:
PR37 merged as `faee3c2f`. Its tested `f3a02aee` tree exactly equals merged main; this PR has been retargeted to main after that proof. Native CI retains `f3a02aee` as its tested baseline.

SSE8 repeatedly checked slice bounds while packing strided rows. Check the final row endpoints once for bounded geometry, load exactly eight bytes per row, pack both lanes directly, and square unsigned byte magnitudes before widening. Odd rows, overlapping read-only inputs, CPU-off operation, and unusual geometry retain their contracts.

On an Apple M4 Max with Go1.27.2, PGO off and one thread, fresh six-order public benchmarks show all nine 8×16 fixtures at **1.625–1.642× prototype parent `1e8809b6`**; all 54 paired samples exceed **1.580×**. Preserve this component win independently of whole-codec timing. Four-row SSE beats the old assembly in these fixtures, while some larger and pointer cases still trail it. This is not a claim of overall assembly parity.

Whole synthetic 720p VP8 measured −0.11% time at 300 frames. The first 60-frame run was +1.45% slower in all six pairs; a fresh separate run was −0.61% with five of six pairs faster. Retain both runs and treat the whole-codec effect as unresolved. All 23 output/allocation fields match with zero allocations.

Add independent scalar comparisons, every ordered byte pair, short-window and alias coverage, and 36 live public benchmarks. The native x64 harness retains all 246 existing controls, adds the new fixtures to both references, and records the changed source hashes. Native x64 results for the exact submitted head are complete below; Rosetta verifies correctness only.

Validation: full native suite, ARM race/checkptr2, x64 checkptr2 and actual AVX-off fallback pass. PGO and repository gates are refreshed before submission. Raw measurements, source variants, failed exploratory runs and detailed scope are retained under `benchmarks/baselines`; README files remain unchanged.

After rebasing, all 228 ARM SSE8 instruction words still match the measured prototype. Combined AMD SSE/subpixel checkptr checks pass, and PGO plus repository gates pass again.

Final exact-head `6a7b1444` results (Go 1.27.2, PGO off):

- On **EPYC 9V74**, all **36 SSE fixtures improve versus main in every pair**. Slice 8×4 gains **1.377–1.404×**, slice 8×8 **1.741–1.744×**, slice 8×16 **1.981–1.984×**, and pointer 8×8 **1.703–1.705×**. All 27 larger/pointer cases exceed 1.5× main in every pair (minimum **1.691×**). Slice APIs beat ASM **1.171–1.428×**; pointer 8×8 still takes **27.47–27.64% more time than ASM**. The original SSE8x8 fixture gains **1.884× main / 1.201× ASM**, all six pairs faster.
- **Whole VP8 regresses +0.8816% versus main in all six pairs**, and remains **+2.2744% versus ASM**. Preserve the verified kernel wins under the requested component-retention policy; no whole-codec gain is claimed. VP9 is unchanged source/control timing: 320 **+0.2969%** versus main (4/6 pairs faster) / **−42.9511% versus ASM**; 720 **−0.3921%** (3/6) / **−50.8906% versus ASM**. Do not infer prior cross-CPU gap closure.
- All **282 kernels × six samples × three variants** have zero bytes/allocations. Eleven source hashes match; **117 targeted checks / 262 PASS lines** include all new SSE tests under selected SIMD and race/checkptr, with no failures/skips. All 22 semantic fields match. Retain the **baseline VP9 720 round3 allocation outlier 1.266667 versus modal1.25**; all current and profile allocation samples match their controls.
- Keep all **91 median regressions and five all-six-slower controls**: three unchanged slice-SAD cases +0.183–0.594%, UV smooth +0.317%, and a two-axis subpixel case +0.134%. Every raw sample remains included. Short profiles do not isolate the cause of whole-codec results.
- Optimized libvpx is a separate **EPYC 7763** job. Fixed-speed VP8 Go takes **2.232940× libvpx time** (+123.2940%; libvpx is faster), matching measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/frame counts without proving bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 +70.1504% and VP9 +197.2228%/+209.8442% compare unequal quality/output work. Every quality-pass output statistic matches its timed output in this job. All reference timers use `vpxenc-stats`; pinned ASM/SSE2/AVX2/runtime dispatch are enabled. Native/C host timings stay separate.

All three exact-head checks pass. Complete byte-preserved native86/C74 raw evidence, audit, source checksums, output/allocation exceptions and scope are retained for the successor archive. No README expansion or dependencies added.

premerge_checks.body:
One-axis motion still executes both bilinear stages. Add one-pass Go SIMD statistics for bounded 16-column tiles when either phase is identity, retaining both original input-window checks, int16 wrapping, read-only aliases and fallbacks. ARM pairs rows with proven int16 difference sums; x64 uses AVX2 and retains upper-state cleanup. Check phases first so ordinary two-axis work skips setup.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go1.27.2, PGO off, six fresh balanced parent/assembly/current rounds over 40 public fixtures:

- The two vertical-only 16×8 fixtures improve **1.534–1.536× versus parent `eb820478`**; all 12 paired samples exceed **1.513×**. They beat old assembly **2.266–2.299×**.
- The other identity/two-axis controls range **0.995–1.017× parent**. Every slower sample is preserved; some larger one-axis sizes still trail assembly.
- Whole synthetic VP8 720p is effectively flat: **−0.0246% time over 300 frames**, **+0.0005% over 60**, with all 23 non-timing fields exact and zero allocations. Assembly still takes less time on these ARM workloads. Keep the correctness-verified ≥1.5× component win independently of whole-codec timing, as required by AGENTS.md.

Parent `eb820478` and merged main `98302461` have identical trees. Full final native suite, scalar/all-phase oracles, 864 unusual-coefficient/alias cases, 48 short-window cases, 40 narrow-sum boundary cases, ARM race/checkptr2, x64 correctness/checkptr and AVX-off fallback pass. All six fixed-speed packet/drop digests match. Selected ARM instruction words match the measured prototype; PGO/fingerprint/noasm/SIMD-selection/pre-commit gates pass.

Native Intel Xeon 8370C measurements of predecessor `1e8809b6` exposed four vertical cases **21–47% slower than main in every pair**. The current repair carries widened AVX2 rows, eliminating a legacy SSE hot-loop copy in the saved optimized x64 build and one repeated widening. Arithmetic and cleanup are unchanged; ARM and x64 horizontal code are unchanged. Correctness/checkptr and repository gates pass. The corrected exact head now passes all three CI checks and the fresh native audit below; the earlier regression remains separately scoped. All predecessor results, including the regressions and the separately scoped C comparison, are preserved in the [predecessor report](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/blob/f3a02aee81979d0c822f5814343f2287d9d86194/benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-amd64/2026-10-18-one-axis-predecessor/REPORT.md).

Require the new axis tests in native and race/checkptr preflight, record nine source hashes, and retain all 246 existing identical native fixtures. Native x64 and optimized-C results for this exact head are complete below. Rosetta remains correctness-only.

Preserve complete benchmark/source archives and PR36’s independently scoped native/C audits, including every regression. README files and dependencies stay clean.

[ARM measurements and proof](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/blob/1e8809b63498b77fb6a347b0c085ebfe3c9aab49/benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-arm64/2026-10-18-subpel-axis/REPORT.md) · [Merged PR36 x64/C audit](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/blob/1e8809b63498b77fb6a347b0c085ebfe3c9aab49/benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-amd64/2026-10-18-pr36-subpel-identity/audit.json)

Final corrected-head evidence for `f3a02aee` (Go 1.27.2, PGO off):

- On **EPYC 7763**, all **16 one-axis fixtures are faster than main and old ASM in every paired sample**. Horizontal medians are **1.206–1.382× main / 2.785–3.541× ASM**; vertical medians **1.248–1.474× main / 2.968–3.653× ASM**. No AMD fixture reaches 1.5× main here; retain the independently qualifying ARM gain without relabeling it. Do not infer a numerical repair speedup from predecessor measurements on Intel.
- All **246 kernels × six samples × three variants** allocate zero bytes/objects. Nine source hashes match; **109 targeted checks / 254 PASS lines** include the axis tests under selected SIMD and race/checkptr, with no failures/skips. All 22 semantic fields and every public/profile allocation sample match; no allocation outlier.
- Whole VP8 time is **−2.0738% versus main** (5/6 pairs faster), **−21.6138% versus ASM**. VP9 320 is **−0.0157% versus main** (4/6) / **−39.8709% versus ASM**; VP9 720 **−0.7230% versus main** (4/6) / **−47.0425% versus ASM**. These results remain CPU/job scoped; no prior 9V74 gap-closure or isolated causal claim.
- Preserve **all 111 median regressions and 75 all-six-slower kernels**. Unchanged controls include Variance16x16 +10.668%, slice-SAD early +5.259–5.540%, Split8x4 +3.779% and several gather8 cases around +2.73–2.86%. Two-axis controls range **0.979–1.011× main**, including slowdowns. Identity controls range **1.006–1.142×**. Every raw pair and output/allocation control remains included.
- Optimized libvpx runs separately on **EPYC 9V45**. Fixed-speed VP8 Go takes **2.114012× libvpx time** (+111.4012%; libvpx is faster), with matched measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/frame counts, without claiming bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 +48.8166% and VP9 +168.2170%/+168.7046% perform unequal quality/output work. **Adaptive C timed payloads include 678205 and 685355 bytes while the quality pass produces 678205**, so its quality metrics do not represent every timed payload. Other quality-pass output statistics match their timing outputs. All reference timers use `vpxenc-stats`; pinned ASM/SSE2/AVX2/runtime dispatch are enabled. Never combine native and C host timings.

The final archive preserves 86 native + 74 C raw files byte for byte, with audit and SHA256 manifests, alongside the rejected predecessor data. The stacked SSE PR is retargeted to main only after this squash merge is proven to have the tested tree; no local checkout/index changes.
